text:
New Jersey is 11-5-0, and the record undersells how well the Devils are playing. They have 59% of the expected goals, allow only 2.51 per hour, and take just 2.56 penalties a game while drawing 3.5. That's a sturdy profile, and our model calls their 22 points almost exactly what they've earned.

Jack Hughes and Jesper Bratt with Arseny Gritsyuk have outscored teams 10-3 at five on five and made 4.02 expected goals per hour. Gritsyuk has 10 points in ten games on 5.9 expected, so some of that will cool. The Nico Hischier line with Timo Meier and Luke Evangelista does the harder work at 61%. On the back end, Luke Hughes and Brett Pesce have been on for 17 goals for and eight against in 257 minutes, though both are also scoring a bit above their chances.

The soft spot is in net. Jake Allen is .881 and 4.4 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, and the team has allowed about six more goals than its chances against suggest. The 5-4 overtime win over St. Louis, after leading 4-1 late in the third, showed both sides of that: the skaters built it, the late defending nearly gave it away. Mike Fink of The Hockey News noted they finished that game with 11 forwards.

A three-game road trip starts tonight on Long Island. Our numbers say 91% for the playoffs.
headline: The Devils are winning the way that lasts
